provenance: Per-unit EDIBLE weight bands for countable foods. Curated from USDA FoodData Central / FNDDS standard portion weights by a multi-agent sweep (2026-08-13), then audited: entries whose band exceeded 3.2x (too wide to catch an error) or that were really multi-modal product families were dropped rather than shipped, and aliases that hijack another food were removed. low_g/high_g are roughly the 10th/90th percentile of a real served unit; the sanity layer clamps into the band rather than overriding with typical_g.

units.name: Apple
units.source: USDA FDC 09003 (Apples, raw, with skin) standard portions: small 149 g, medium (3" dia) 182 g, large 223 g; high end extended for large Honeycrisp/Fuji retail sizes.

units.name: Avocado (half)
units.source: USDA FDC 09038 (Avocados, raw, California): 1 fruit without skin and seed 136 g, so half ~68 g; all-commercial-varieties fruit 201 g gives a larger half.

units.name: Avocado (whole, flesh only)
units.source: USDA FDC 09038; Hass flesh 136 g, all-varieties 201 g.

units.name: Baby carrot
units.source: USDA FDC 11124 portion data: 1 medium baby carrot 10 g, 1 large baby carrot 15 g.

units.name: Bacon strip
units.source: USDA: bacon, pork, cooked (pan-fried), 1 medium slice = 8 g; thick-cut cooked ~12-13 g

units.name: Bagel
units.source: USDA FDC 'Bagels, plain, enriched' 1 medium (3-1/2 to 4 in dia) = 98 g; 1 large (4-1/2 in) = 131 g; 1 mini = 26 g.

units.name: Banana
units.source: USDA FDC 09040 (Bananas, raw) standard portions, peel removed: small 101 g, medium (7"-7 7/8") 118 g, large 136 g, extra large 152 g.

units.name: Bread slice
units.source: USDA FDC 'Bread, white, commercially prepared' 1 slice = 25 g, 1 large slice = 32-38 g, 1 thin slice = 20 g; 'Bread, whole-wheat' 1 slice = 28-32 g.

units.name: Breakfast sausage link
units.source: USDA SR: pork sausage, cooked link (4 in x 7/8 in) ~ 26-27 g; retail cooked breakfast links label at 24-27 g

units.name: Brownie
units.source: USDA FDC 'Brownies, commercially prepared' standard portion 1 square (2-3/4 x 7/8 in) = 56 g; bakery/cafe brownies commonly 80-110 g.

units.name: Burger patty, quarter-pound
units.source: 4 oz (113 g) raw is the standard quarter-pound spec; ~25% cook loss -> ~85 g cooked

units.name: Buttermilk biscuit
units.source: USDA FDC 'Biscuits, plain or buttermilk, commercially baked' 1 biscuit (2-1/2 in dia) = 51 g; 1 large (3 in dia) = 82-101 g.

units.name: Carrot (whole)
units.source: USDA FDC 11124 (Carrots, raw): small 50 g, medium (7 1/2" long) 61 g, large 72 g.

units.name: Cheese cube (1 inch)
units.source: USDA SR: cheddar cheese, 1 cubic inch = 17.3 g; other firm cheeses 16-18 g per cubic inch

units.name: Cherry tomato
units.source: USDA FDC 11529 (Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw): 1 cherry tomato 17 g; grape tomatoes commonly 8-10 g.

units.name: Chicken drumstick
units.source: USDA SR: drumstick, meat and skin, roasted, bone removed = 52 g. Breaded/fried and larger modern birds push higher.

units.name: Chicken nugget
units.source: McDonald's 20-piece McNuggets = 323 g -> ~16 g/piece; retail frozen nuggets label out at 15-20 g each

units.name: Chicken satay skewer
units.source: Thai/Indonesian restaurant appetizer portions (4-6 skewers from 180-250 g of meat) and yakitori standard skewer weights

units.name: Chicken tender / strip
units.source: FNDDS 'chicken tenders or strips, breaded, from restaurant'; foodservice specs commonly 1.5-2.2 oz per cooked piece. Frozen retail tenders run smaller (~30 g).

units.name: Chicken thigh
units.source: USDA SR: thigh, meat and skin, roasted, bone removed = 62 g. Retail boneless thighs run 4-6 oz raw (113-170 g) -> ~85-130 g cooked.

units.name: Chicken wing (one piece: drumette or flat)

units.source: No USDA standard portion; established confectionery references and major boxed-chocolate producers -- individual truffles 10-15 g, Lindt Lindor ball 12.5 g, large hand-rolled truff

units.name: Cinnamon roll
units.source: USDA FDC 'Sweet rolls, cinnamon, commercially prepared with raisins' 1 roll = 60 g; bakery cinnamon rolls with icing 110-150 g. Mall-style oversize rolls (e.g. Cinnabon Classic ~22

units.name: Corn on the cob
units.source: USDA FDC 168537/169998 (Corn, sweet, yellow, raw/cooked): kernels from 1 small ear 73 g, medium ear (6 3/4"-7 1/2") 90 g, large ear 118 g.

units.name: Croissant
units.source: USDA FDC 'Croissants, butter' (FDC 174987) 1 medium = 57 g, 1 large = 67 g, 1 mini = 28 g; artisan bakery croissants 70-90 g.

units.name: Cupcake
units.source: USDA FDC 'Cake, snack cakes, not chocolate, with icing' and FNDDS cupcake with frosting entries: ~50-73 g for a standard 2-1/2 in cupcake; bakery cupcakes with piped buttercream 90

units.name: Danish pastry
units.source: USDA FDC 'Danish pastry, cheese' 1 pastry (4-1/4 in dia) = 71 g; 'Danish pastry, fruit' 1 pastry = 71-94 g; bakery danishes 90-115 g.

units.name: Dinner sausage link (Italian / bratwurst / kielbasa)
units.source: Retail links pack 5 per 19-20 oz (~108 g raw each) or 4 oz raw (113 g); ~20% cook loss -> ~85-90 g cooked

units.name: Donut
units.source: USDA FDC 'Doughnuts, yeast-leavened, glazed' 1 medium (3-3/4 in dia) = 60 g; 'Doughnuts, cake-type, plain' 1 medium (3-1/4 in) = 47 g. Krispy Kreme original glazed 49 g, Dunkin gla

units.name: Dumpling / gyoza
units.source: FNDDS dumpling/potsticker entries (~20-25 g each cooked) and frozen-brand per-piece weights (Ling Ling, Bibigo, Trader Joe's: 19-26 g)

units.name: Egg roll
units.source: USDA FNDDS egg roll standard portion (~89 g per roll) and Chinese-American takeout per-piece weights

units.name: English muffin
units.source: USDA FDC 18314 English muffin, plain, 57 g.

units.name: Falafel ball
units.source: USDA SR falafel patty, approx 2-1/4 inch diameter = 17 g; Mediterranean restaurant and frozen-brand balls run 22-32 g

units.name: Fish finger / fish stick
units.source: US retail labels (Gorton's, Van de Kamp's): 6 sticks = 170 g -> 28 g each; UK fish fingers 25-28 g each

units.name: Grape (single)
units.source: USDA FDC 09132 (Grapes, red or green, European type, raw): 10 grapes 49 g, i.e. ~4.9 g each.

units.name: Hot dog (frankfurter, no bun)
units.source: Standard US retail 8-per-pound frank = 57 g raw -> ~50 g cooked; USDA frankfurter, beef, 1 frank = 45 g; bun-length/jumbo 6-per-pound = 76 g raw

units.name: Kiwi
units.source: USDA FDC 09148 (Kiwifruit, green, raw): 1 fruit (2" dia) 69 g, edible flesh without skin.

units.name: Large egg
units.source: USDA FDC / SR Legacy standard portion: large egg, whole, raw, without shell = 50 g (medium 44 g, extra-large 56 g, jumbo 63 g)

units.name: Lemon bar (traybake square)
units.source: No dedicated USDA standard portion; anchored to USDA FNDDS 'Lemon bar' ~2 in square (~55-65 g) and cafe traybake squares commonly cut 2.5-3 in (80-100 g).

units.name: Lemon or lime wedge
units.source: USDA FDC 09150/09159 (Lemons/limes, raw): 1 wedge or slice (1/8 of a 2 1/8" dia lemon) 7 g; lime wedge ~8 g.

units.name: Macaron
units.source: No USDA standard portion; established patisserie references -- standard Parisian macaron shell pair with ganache 12-15 g, Laduree/Pierre Herme size ~17-20 g, petit format ~8-10 g.

units.name: Mandarin
units.source: USDA FDC 09218 (Tangerines/mandarins, raw): small 76 g, medium (2 1/2" dia) 88 g, large 120 g; clementine 74 g.

units.name: Muffin
units.source: USDA FDC 'Muffins, blueberry, commercially prepared' 1 small (2-1/2 in dia) = 57-66 g, 1 large = 139 g; coffee-chain muffins typically 110-140 g.

units.name: Olive
units.source: USDA FDC 09193/09195 (Olives, ripe canned; green pickled): small 3.2 g, large 4.4 g, jumbo 8.3 g, super colossal ~12 g.

units.name: Orange
units.source: USDA FDC 09200 (Oranges, raw, navels) 1 orange 140 g; 09200/09201 all commercial varieties small 96 g, medium 131 g, large 184 g.

units.name: Pancake
units.source: USDA FDC 'Pancakes, plain, prepared from recipe' 1 pancake (4 in dia) = 38 g; (6 in dia) = 77 g; diner pancakes 90-110 g.

units.name: Peach
units.source: USDA FDC 09236 (Peaches, raw): small 130 g, medium (2 2/3" dia) 150 g, large 175 g; nectarine (09266) medium 142 g.

units.name: Pear
units.source: USDA FDC 09252 (Pears, raw): small 148 g, medium 178 g, large 230 g.

units.name: Pizza slice, deep dish
units.source: Chicago deep-dish restaurant menu weights (1/8 of a large pie, 220-290 g), Detroit-style square weights (130-160 g), and Pizza Hut pan slice data (~115-135 g)

units.name: Pizza slice, hand-tossed
units.source: USDA FNDDS regular-crust pizza slice (~107 g) and chain data (Domino's large hand-tossed cheese slice ~112 g; NY counter slice, 1/8 of an 18-inch pie, 140-165 g)

units.name: Pizza slice, thin crust
units.source: USDA FoodData Central thin-crust pizza portions (1 piece NFS = 97 g for frozen thin crust) and 1/8-of-14-inch restaurant slice weights

units.name: Plum
units.source: USDA FDC 09279 (Plums, raw): 1 fruit (2 1/8" dia) 66 g; 1 cup sliced 165 g.

units.name: Potato
units.source: USDA FDC 170026 (Potatoes, russet, flesh and skin, raw): small 138 g, medium (2 1/4"-3 1/4" dia) 173 g, large 369 g.

units.name: Roma tomato
units.source: USDA FDC 11529 plum/roma tomato 62 g.

units.name: Scone
units.source: No single USDA standard portion; FNDDS scone entries ~60 g, British plain scone 55-70 g, US coffee-chain scones (e.g. Starbucks) 100-120 g.

units.name: Sea scallop
units.source: Count sizing: 20/30 per lb = 15-23 g raw each; restaurant 10/20 count = 23-45 g raw; ~15-20% cook loss

units.name: Shrimp, large / jumbo
units.source: Industry count sizing: 31/35 to 21/25 per lb headless shell-on = 13-21 g raw each; ~70-75% edible yield after peel and cook

units.name: Shrimp, medium
units.source: Industry count sizing: 41/50 per lb headless shell-on = 9-11 g raw each; peeling + cooking yields ~70% edible

units.name: Slice of cake
units.source: USDA FDC 'Cake, chocolate, commercially prepared with chocolate frosting' 1 piece (1/8 of an 18 oz cake) = 64 g; restaurant layer-cake slices commonly 150-200 g.

units.name: Slice of cheese
units.source: Kraft-style processed single = 19-21 g; USDA cheddar, 1 slice (1 oz) = 28 g; deli-cut slices 25-34 g

units.name: Slice of cheesecake
units.source: USDA FDC 'Cheesecake, commercially prepared' 1 piece (1/6 of a 17 oz cake) = 80 g; restaurant slices 150-200 g (Cheesecake Factory slices exceed 200 g).

units.name: Slice of pie
units.source: USDA FDC 'Pie, apple, commercially prepared' 1 piece (1/8 of 9 in pie) = 117-125 g; 1 piece (1/6 of 8 in pie) = ~155 g; diner slices 170-200 g.

units.name: Smash / thin fast-food patty
units.source: Smash patties are typically 2 oz (57 g) raw -> ~45 g cooked; classic fast-food regular hamburger patty 1.6 oz raw -> ~30 g cooked; sliders 1-1.5 oz raw

units.name: Strawberry
units.source: USDA FDC 09316 (Strawberries, raw): small 7 g, medium (1 1/4" dia) 12 g, large 18 g, extra large 27 g.

units.name: Sushi nigiri piece
units.source: USDA FNDDS sushi entries (~30-35 g per nigiri piece) cross-checked against sushi-bar build standards: 18-20 g shari (rice) + 10-15 g neta (topping)

units.name: Sweet potato
units.source: USDA FDC 168482 (Sweet potato, raw, unprepared): medium (5" long, 2" dia) 130 g, large 180 g; baked in skin medium 114 g.

units.name: Taco
units.source: Chain nutrition data (Taco Bell crunchy taco 78 g, soft taco 99 g) plus taqueria street-taco and sit-down restaurant taco weights

units.name: Tomato (whole)
units.source: USDA FDC 11529 medium whole tomato 123 g.

units.name: Tortilla chip
units.source: Standard 1 oz (28 g) reference serving = 10-12 chips per Doritos/Tostitos labels, giving 2.3-2.8 g per chip
